relationships.subject: G9a
relationships.evidence_quote: In fact, nerve injury consistently increased the G9a action and thus the levels of H3K9me2 in the promoter of the OPRM1 gene in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG); this resulted in condensed chromatin and gene silencing and a diminished opioid analgesic effect.

relationships.subject: C/EBPβ
relationships.evidence_quote: C/EBPβ was shown to indirectly inhibit MOR and the voltage-gated K+ channel Kv1.2 abundance in the ipsilateral DRG by activating the G9a gene (EHMT2)

relationships.subject: miR-219
relationships.evidence_quote: One study demonstrated that this process, which contributes to the development of chronic tolerance to morphine analgesia in mouse DRG, was mediated by miR-219 by targeting CaMKIIγ [26].

relationships.subject: miR-339-3p
relationships.evidence_quote: Then, it was demonstrated that miR-339-3p destabilizes MOR mRNA and thus inhibits the MOR protein biosynthesis [25].

key_findings: Review: opioids alter DNA methylation, histone marks and miRNAs in pain and reward circuits (e.g. G9a/H3K9me2 silencing of OPRM1 in DRG).
Morphine alters BDNF methylation and transcription, with miR-219/CaMKIIγ implicated in tolerance.
